requirements.subject: ent:receiving-operation
requirements.canonical: A receiving operation consists of a receive part and an optional assignment part.
requirements.original: A receiving operation consists of a receive part and an (optional) assignment part.

requirements.subject: ent:receive-part
requirements.canonical: The receive part of a receiving operation SHALL specify the port at which the operation takes place.
requirements.original: a) specifies the port at which the operation shall take place;

requirements.subject: ent:receive-part
requirements.canonical: The receive part of a receiving operation MAY contain a matching part that specifies the acceptable input matching the operation.
requirements.original: b) defines an optional matching part which specifies the acceptable input which will match the statement;

requirements.subject: ent:receive-part
requirements.canonical: The receive part of a receiving operation MAY contain an address expression that uniquely identifies the communication partner in one-to-many connections.
requirements.original: c) gives an optional address expression that uniquely identifies the communication partner (in case of one-to-many connections).

requirements.subject: ent:receiving-operation
requirements.canonical: A receiving operation SHALL contain the port name and the operation name.
requirements.original: The port name and operation name shall be present.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-part
requirements.canonical: The matching part of a receiving operation NEED NOT be present unless the content of the received communication is to be restricted.
requirements.original: The matching part needs only be present if the content of the received communication shall be restricted.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: The identification of the communication partner (`from` clause) in a receiving operation NEED NOT be specified except in one-to-many connections where the communication partner needs to be explicitly identified.
requirements.original: The identification of the communication partner (denoted by the from keyword) is optional and need only be specified in cases of one-to-many connections where the receiving entity needs to be explicitly identified.

ambiguity.issue: The text says "receiving entity" although the entity identified by the from clause is the sending communication partner.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-part
requirements.canonical: The assignment part of a receiving operation MAY be omitted.
requirements.original: The assignment part in a receiving operation is optional.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-part
requirements.canonical: For message-based ports, the assignment part of a receiving operation stores the received message.
requirements.original: For message-based ports it is used when it is required to store received messages.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-part
requirements.canonical: For procedure-based ports, the assignment part of a receiving operation stores the `in` and `inout` parameters of an accepted call, the return value or the exception.
requirements.original: In the case of procedure-based ports it is used for storing the in and inout parameters of an accepted call, for storing the return value or for storing exceptions.

ambiguity.issue: Only getcall stores in/inout parameters; getreply stores out/inout parameters, which the sentence does not mention. Chosen reading: the text lists examples per operation kind.
readings: The assignment part of a getcall operation stores in and inout parameters, that of a getreply operation the return value (and out/inout parameters), and that of a catch operation the exception.
The assignment part of any procedure-based receiving operation stores only in and inout parameters, return values or exceptions.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-part
requirements.canonical: Strong typing IS NOT required for the message or parameter value assignment part of a receiving operation.
requirements.original: For the message or parameter value assignment part strong typing is not required, e.g. the variable used for storing a message shall be type-compatible to the type of the incoming message.

ambiguity.issue: "strong typing is not required" followed by "e.g. ... shall be type-compatible" is contradictory in wording; chosen reading: type compatibility instead of type identity is sufficient.
readings: The variable in a value or parameter assignment SHALL be type-compatible with, but need not be of the same type as, the received value.
No type check is performed for value or parameter assignments of a receiving operation.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: The variable used for storing a received message SHALL be type-compatible with the type of the incoming message.
requirements.original: For the message or parameter value assignment part strong typing is not required, e.g. the variable used for storing a message shall be type-compatible to the type of the incoming message.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-part
requirements.canonical: The assignment part of a receiving operation MAY assign the sender address of a message, exception, reply or call to a variable.
requirements.original: In addition, the assignment part may also be used to assign the sender address of a message, exception, reply or call to a variable.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-assignment
requirements.canonical: Storing the sender address IS useful in one-to-many connections where the same message or call can be received from different components but the response has to be sent back to the original sending component.
requirements.original: This is useful for one-to-many connections where, for example, the same message or call can be received from different components, but the message, reply or exception shall be sent back to the original sending component.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-part
requirements.condition: the receiving operation uses any from a port array
requirements.canonical: For a receiving operation using `any from` on a port array, the assignment part MAY store the indices that identify the port instance where the receiving operation matched.
requirements.original: For receiving operations using the any port from a port array construction (see clause 22.2.2), the assignment part may also be used to store the indices that identify the specific port instance where the receiving operation matched.

requirements.subject: ent:nodefault-modifier
requirements.condition: the receiving operation is used as a stand-alone statement
requirements.canonical: If a receiving operation is used as a stand-alone statement, the `@nodefault` modifier MAY be placed before it.
requirements.original: If a receiving operation is used as a stand-alone statement, the @nodefault modifier can be placed before it to indicate that the implicit alt statement containing the operation as an alternative shall have the @nodefault modifier.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.condition: a @nodefault modifier precedes a stand-alone receiving operation
requirements.canonical: If a `@nodefault` modifier is placed before a stand-alone receiving operation, the implicit `alt` statement containing the operation as an alternative SHALL have the `@nodefault` modifier.
requirements.original: If a receiving operation is used as a stand-alone statement, the @nodefault modifier can be placed before it to indicate that the implicit alt statement containing the operation as an alternative shall have the @nodefault modifier.
